# cell-sphere-game

<p align="center">

`cell-sphere-game` is an autonomous incremental game about watching life find a
foothold, spread across a finite world, endure worsening conditions, and finally
disappear. You do not command organisms or click to keep them alive. Your most
important choices happen after extinction, when the completed World becomes
History and its Echoes can strengthen the Worlds that follow.

The game runs directly in a modern browser. Its simulation, planet, clouds, stars,
cell materials, and progression geography are generated by the project itself.

## A World in one breath

```text
birth → expansion → scarcity → pressure → extinction → memory → evolution → rebirth
```

Every World begins at **Environment Level 0**. Life establishes itself in a
favorable local niche and expands through neighboring cells, drawing on finite
local resources as it goes. Environment pressure rises with authoritative World
time, gradually changing resource yield, renewal, climate, toxicity, maintenance,
and transport.

A World ends through ecological failure rather than a detached timer or scripted
disaster. The Result records the realized **SCORE**, **Echoes**, **Trophies**, and
**History** produced by that run. Spend Echoes in **Evolution**, begin again, and
see how the same underlying rules behave with a different permanent inheritance.

## What the player does

- Start a World and let its ecology act on its own.
- Rotate and zoom the planet to follow growth, stress, fragmentation, and remains.
- Inspect the current World, Environment pressure, and recorded History.
- Choose a foreground simulation pace from 0.25× through 1.5×.
- After extinction, strengthen one exact Evolution cell at a time.
- Continue manually, or leave Result untouched and let the next World begin.

World cells are not units to micromanage. The central skill is reading the planet,
understanding why a lineage succeeded or failed, and deciding what future Worlds
should inherit.

## The living sphere

The planet is not a flat board wrapped in a globe effect. Whole spherical cells
are the shared units of geography, ecology, transformation, resources, and
Luminous bioelectric state.

Ordinary life is communicated mainly through cell boundaries, so terrain and
finite resources remain visible beneath it. Growth fronts, internal populations,
stress, critical state, remains, selection, coastlines, and Luminous charge each
retain a distinct visual meaning.

Home and World sit inside a deterministic orbital composition of deep space,
varied stars, moving planetary clouds, and rare shooting stars. These effects are
presentation only: they never change simulation state, SCORE, progression, or
History.

## Evolution

Evolution is a second cellular planet and the permanent progression surface. Its
**2,562 visible cells** are all real progression units rather than decorative
territory.

A fresh profile begins at the **First Division** root. Owning a cell exposes its
direct neighbors, and every purchase raises exactly one cell by one local level.
The sphere carries **42 authored archetypes** across seven connected domains.
Repeated cells of the same archetype contribute to one shared rank and one bounded
effect sequence.

The immutable continents, oceans, relief, lakes, and biomes guide the layout and
make progression feel geographical. They do not secretly change costs, rewards,
or mechanical effect strength.

## Controls

| Goal | Mouse or touch | Keyboard |
|---|---|---|
| Turn the globe | Drag the globe or an available **Drag globe** strip | — |
| Zoom | Wheel or pinch | — |
| Inspect or select a visible cell | Click or tap | — |
| Move across Evolution cells | Click or tap a cell | <kbd>←</kbd>/<kbd>→</kbd> by cell number |
| Return to First Division | Select it on the globe | <kbd>Home</kbd> |
| Move among ready Evolution cells | Select them on the globe | <kbd>Page Up</kbd>/<kbd>Page Down</kbd> |

A deliberate release can carry the globe with inertia; inactivity can begin a
slow automatic orbit on Home and World. Reduced Motion removes inertia, automatic
orbit, cloud travel, and shooting-star travel without changing authoritative
gameplay.

## Deterministic by design

The project keeps simulation authority separate from presentation:

```text
immutable World inputs
        ↓
fixed-step simulation authority
        ↓
immutable observable snapshots
        ↓
WebGL2 or Canvas 2D presentation
```

- The same immutable inputs produce the same authoritative World.
- Speed changes how quickly complete ticks are delivered, never what a tick means.
- Worker and main-thread fallback execution share the same simulation authority.
- Camera motion, frame cadence, quality, visibility, and renderer choice cannot
  alter ecology, SCORE, Echoes, or Evolution.
- Closing the page does not advance a World, and no offline progress is promised.

History is the durable temporal surface. When a compatible local visual
checkpoint exists it can reconstruct the globe approximately; otherwise History
remains an honest semantic record rather than inventing unavailable visuals.

## Rendering and accessibility

WebGL2 is the primary renderer, with Canvas 2D as a semantic fallback. Both consume
the same cell meanings even when their exact pixels differ. The interface also
supports responsive layouts, touch, keyboard navigation, reduced motion, forced
colors, and textual equivalents for important non-color state.

The deployed application has no runtime package dependencies or bitmap textures.
The visual world is procedural; the small hand-authored project mark is its only
runtime image asset. The Home capture above is documentation only.

## Run locally

Requirements: **Node.js 22 or newer**. No dependency installation or build step is
required.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/lkjsxc/cell-sphere-game.git
cd cell-sphere-game
npm run serve
```

Open <http://localhost:8080/>.

A containerized server is also available:

```bash
docker compose up serve
```

## Verification

Run the complete fast local gate:

```bash
npm run verify
```

This covers repository structure, identity, unit and integration tests,
deterministic simulation audits, fair-agent smoke runs, balance checks,
performance benchmarks, and static links. Browser verification requires Chrome:

```bash
npm run test:browser
```

Useful focused commands include `npm test`, `npm run balance:smoke`, and
`npm run benchmark`. See
[`docs/testing.md`](https://github.com/lkjsxc/cell-sphere-game/blob/main/docs/testing.md)
for the full matrix.
